partners.diseaseBName: mitochondrial complex I deficiency, nuclear type 4
partners.mechanism_chain: Pathogenic variant in CYCS (HGNC:2503) —DISRUPTS→ CYCS (HGNC:2503); CYCS (HGNC:2503) —BINDS→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0045224); Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0045224) —DECREASES→ ATP production (CHEBI:15422); ATP production (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial disease (HP:0003152); Pathogenic variant in NDUFV1 (HGNC:7773) —DISRUPTS→ NDUFV1 (HGNC:7773); NDUFV1 (HGNC:7773) —BINDS→ Mitochondrial complex I assembly/function (GO:0005746); Mitochondrial complex I assembly/function (GO:0005746) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0045224). Loss-of-function variants in CYCS (associated with disease A) and NDUFV1 (associated with disease B) both converge on the mitochondrial electron transport chain. NDUFV1 is a core component of Complex I, directly impacting its function. CYCS, while a soluble protein, is crucial for electron transfer within the electron transport chain and also plays a role in apoptosis. Impairment of Complex I function by NDUFV1 mutations leads to reduced ATP production. Similarly, disruption of CYCS function can also impair electron transport and ATP synthesis. Therefore, both disease modules converge on the compromised function of the mitochondrial electron transport chain, leading to reduced ATP production and the downstream phenotype of mitochondrial disease.
